name: Argonauta (80)
subtitle: 80-gun Ship of the Line
description: Built at Ferrol in 1798, the 80-gun ship of the line Argonauta served as the flagship of Lieutenant General Federico Gravina during the 1805 West Indies expedition and at the Battle of Cape Finisterre, where she led the Allied van squadron into action against Admiral Robert Calder's British fleet.

markers.damage: Mizzen and fore masts knocked down, Masts and spars Cutwater torn down
markers.notes: Led the Franco-Spanish line of battle at the head of the van division.

markers.damage: Rudder disabled, hull pierced near the waterline; scuttled during the post-battle gale

name: San Rafael (80)
subtitle: 80-gun Ship of the Line
description: An 80-gun Spanish ship of the line launched at Havana in 1771. At the Battle of Cape Finisterre on July 22, 1805, San Rafael fought fiercely in the thick fog within Gravina's van division until she was dismasted and captured by the British fleet.

markers.damage: Completely dismasted and heavily hulled; captured by the Royal Navy

name: Firme (74)
subtitle: 74-gun Ship of the Line
description: A 74-gun Spanish ship of the line built at La Carraca (Cádiz) in 1754. During the Battle of Cape Finisterre she sustained severe concentrated fire from several British ships of the line, losing all her masts before striking her colors.

markers.damage: Main and mizzen masts shot away; captured after heavy close-range combat

name: Bucentaure (80)
subtitle: 80-gun Bucentaure-class Ship of the Line
description: Lead ship of her class of 80-gun ships of the line of the French Navy, launched at Toulon in 1803. Bucentaure served as the flagship of Vice-Admiral Pierre-Charles Villeneuve at both the Battle of Cape Finisterre and the Battle of Trafalgar.

markers.damage: Light damage to sails and rigging in dense fog
Completely dismasted after raking broadsides from HMS Victory and HMS Neptune

name: HMS Prince of Wales (98)
subtitle: 98-gun Boyne-class Second Rate Ship of the Line
description: A 98-gun second-rate ship of the line of the Royal Navy launched at Portsmouth Dockyard in 1794. HMS Prince of Wales served as the flagship of Vice-Admiral Sir Robert Calder at the Battle of Cape Finisterre on July 22, 1805.

name: 1er Régiment de Grenadiers-à-Pied de la Garde Impériale
subtitle: Old Guard Infantry Regiment
description: The senior infantry regiment of Napoleon's Old Guard. Formed from the most battle-hardened veterans of the Grande Armée, the 1st Foot Grenadiers formed the final reserve at the Battle of Waterloo, holding squares near La Belle Alliance to cover the French retreat.

markers.role: Imperial Guard Reserve (Rossomme / La Belle Alliance)
markers.damage: Maintained square formation under heavy Allied artillery and cavalry pressure during the final retreat

name: Federico Gravina
subtitle: Captain General of the Royal Spanish Armada
description: Federico Carlos Gravina y Nápoli (1756–1806) was Spain's premier naval commander during the Napoleonic Wars. At the Battle of Cape Finisterre (July 22, 1805), commanding from the 80-gun Argonauta, his Spanish van division bore the brunt of the fighting in thick fog. Months later he commanded the Spanish fleet at Trafalgar, where he was mortally wounded.

markers.role: Commander of the Allied Van Squadron
markers.strength: 6 Spanish Ships of the Line (Van Division)
markers.damage: Two ships of the van (San Rafael and Firme) dismasted and captured in dense fog

markers.role: Commander of the Spanish Squadron (Príncipe de Asturias)
markers.damage: Severely wounded in the left arm by grapeshot aboard Príncipe de Asturias

name: Pierre-Charles Villeneuve
subtitle: Vice-Admiral of the French Navy
description: Pierre-Charles-Jean-Baptiste-Silvestre de Villeneuve (1763–1806) commanded the combined Franco-Spanish fleet during the 1805 Atlantic campaign, leading the fleet at the Battle of Cape Finisterre against Sir Robert Calder and subsequently at the Battle of Trafalgar against Lord Nelson.

markers.strength: 20 Ships of the Line (14 French, 6 Spanish), 7 Frigates
markers.damage: 2 Spanish ships captured; allied fleet put into Vigo and Ferrol

markers.strength: 33 Ships of the Line (18 French, 15 Spanish)
markers.damage: Flagship Bucentaure dismasted and forced to strike; Villeneuve taken prisoner

name: Sir Robert Calder
subtitle: Vice-Admiral of the Royal Navy
description: Admiral Sir Robert Calder, 1st Baronet (1745–1818) commanded the British blockading squadron off Ferrol that intercepted Villeneuve's returning Franco-Spanish fleet at the Battle of Cape Finisterre on July 22, 1805, capturing two Spanish ships of the line despite being outnumbered 15 to 20.

markers.strength: 15 Ships of the Line, 2 Frigates, 2 Smaller Vessels
markers.damage: HMS Windsor Castle crippled; captured Spanish ships San Rafael and Firme

name: Jean-Martin Petit
subtitle: Général de Brigade, Commander of the 1st Foot Grenadiers of the Old Guard
description: Baron Jean-Martin Petit (1772–1856) was famous for being embraced by Napoleon during the Emperor's farewell to the Old Guard at Fontainebleau in 1814. At Waterloo on June 18, 1815, he commanded the 1st Regiment of Foot Grenadiers of the Imperial Guard, holding the final squares covering the army's withdrawal.

markers.damage: Covered the French retreat in square formation until nightfall

name: Terrible (74)
subtitle: 74-gun Ship of the Line
description: Built at Ferrol in 1798, the 80-gun ship of the line Argonauta served as the flagship of Lieutenant General Federico Gravina during the 1805 West Indies expedition and at the Battle of Cape Finisterre, where she led the Allied van squadron into action against Admiral Robert Calder's British fleet.

markers.role: Served as the second ship in the vanguard
markers.damage: Rigging Much torn, two cannons dismounted, slide ripped off, one shot flotation high
markers.notes: Served in the vanguard and bore the brunt of the British attack.

markers.damage: Rudder disabled, hull pierced near the waterline; scuttled during the post-battle gale

name: América (64)
subtitle: 64-gun Ship of the Line
description: The América was a 64-gun Spanish Navy ship of the line built in Havana in 1766 and decommissioned in 1823. Measuring 61.81 meters long with a 1,178-ton displacement, this two-decked vessel carried a crew of 776 men and was armed with a mix of cannons and howitzers.

markers.role: Served as the third ship in the vanguard
markers.damage: All masts bullet-riddled, 60 shots in masts
markers.notes: Served in the vanguard and held the vanguard line in heavy fog, suffering heavy damage.

name: España (64)
subtitle: 64-gun Ship of the Line
description: España was a Spanish 64-gun ship of the line launched in 1757. She escorted treasure fleets to New Spain and fought at Gibraltar, Cape Spartel, and Finisterre before being scrapped in 1808.

markers.role: Served as the third ship in the vanguard
markers.damage: Riggig much torn, mizzen mast down, several spars, Rudder partly obliterated, some damage in hull.
markers.notes: Suffered heavy damage, taking 28 casualties before retreating to Vigo.
